+
+## Review trace
+
+`agent.Trace` records each model call, tool call, and task outcome of an
+agentic review, in order. Sub-agents call tools through `Trace.Dispatch`.
+The runner adds task outcomes when its `Trace` field is set. `Trace.File` writes
+a `review.TraceFile` pinned to the head SHA. Pass it to the exporter with
+`px1 export-review --trace-file trace.json`. The report then shows a
+**How px1 reviewed this** section: the tier, spend, any exhausted budget,
+task outcomes, and an expandable list of every step.
+
+| Recorded | Not recorded |
+| --- | --- |
+| Tool name, arguments (512 bytes), result size, truncation, a 512-byte result preview, and elapsed time | Linked-issue content: reports can be shared more widely than the tracker it came from |
+| Model role and settled token counts | Prompts, model output, and provider error text |
+| Task outcome and its generic reason | Anything past 2,000 events, which is counted as `dropped` |
+
+The exporter rejects a trace for any other revision, a Base tier, unknown
+fields, out-of-order sequence numbers, or oversized text. The report renders
+every trace string as text, never markup. The section states that the log shows
+what px1 looked at, not that unexamined code is correct.

index 0000000..f1ff406
--- /dev/null
+++ b/internal/hosted/review/trace.go
@@ -0,0 +1,88 @@
+package review
+
+import (
+	"bytes"
+	"encoding/json"
+	"errors"
+	"fmt"
+	"io"
+	"strings"
+)
+
+const (
+	MaxTraceEvents      = 2_000
+	MaxTraceDetailBytes = 512
+	MaxTracePreview     = 512
+)
+
+// TraceEvent is one step of an agentic review: a model call, a tool call, or
+// a finished sub-agent task. It records what was asked and how much came back,
+// never provider error text, and never linked-issue content.
+type TraceEvent struct {
+	Seq          int    `json:"seq"`
+	Agent        string `json:"agent"`
+	Kind         string `json:"kind"`
+	Name         string `json:"name"`
+	Detail       string `json:"detail,omitempty"`
+	Preview      string `json:"preview,omitempty"`
+	ResultBytes  int    `json:"result_bytes,omitempty"`
+	Truncated    bool   `json:"truncated,omitempty"`
+	Failed       bool   `json:"failed,omitempty"`
+	InputTokens  int64  `json:"input_tokens,omitempty"`
+	OutputTokens int64  `json:"output_tokens,omitempty"`
+	ElapsedMS    int64  `json:"elapsed_ms"`
+}
+
+type TraceSpend struct {
+	InputTokens  int64  `json:"input_tokens"`
+	OutputTokens int64  `json:"output_tokens"`
+	CostMicrousd int64  `json:"cost_microusd"`
+	ModelCalls   int    `json:"model_calls"`
+	ToolCalls    int    `json:"tool_calls"`
+	Exhausted    string `json:"exhausted,omitempty"`
+}
+
+// TraceFile is the revision-pinned record rendered as "How px1 reviewed this".
+type TraceFile struct {
+	Revision string       `json:"revision"`
+	Tier     string       `json:"tier"`
+	Spend    TraceSpend   `json:"spend"`
+	Events   []TraceEvent `json:"events"`
+	Dropped  int          `json:"dropped,omitempty"`
+}
+
+var traceKinds = map[string]bool{"model": true, "tool": true, "task": true}
+
+// DecodeTraceFile accepts a trace only for the exact report head and within
+// the event and text bounds a recorder can produce.
+func DecodeTraceFile(data []byte, head string) (TraceFile, error) {
+	decoder := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(data))
+	decoder.DisallowUnknownFields()
+	var trace TraceFile
+	if err := decoder.Decode(&trace); err != nil {
+		return TraceFile{}, fmt.Errorf("decode review trace: %w", err)
+	}
+	if _, err := decoder.Token(); err != io.EOF {
+		return TraceFile{}, errors.New("review trace contains trailing data")
+	}
+	if trace.Revision != head {
+		return TraceFile{}, errors.New("review trace revision does not match report head")
+	}
+	if trace.Tier != "plus" && trace.Tier != "apex" {
+		return TraceFile{}, errors.New("review trace tier must be plus or apex")
+	}
+	if len(trace.Events) > MaxTraceEvents || trace.Dropped < 0 {
+		return TraceFile{}, fmt.Errorf("review trace exceeds %d events", MaxTraceEvents)
+	}
+	for i, event := range trace.Events {
+		if event.Seq != i+1 || !traceKinds[event.Kind] || strings.TrimSpace(event.Agent) == "" || strings.TrimSpace(event.Name) == "" ||
+			len(event.Agent) > 200 || len(event.Name) > 100 || len(event.Detail) > MaxTraceDetailBytes || len(event.Preview) > MaxTracePreview ||
+			event.ResultBytes < 0 || event.InputTokens < 0 || event.OutputTokens < 0 || event.ElapsedMS < 0 {
+			return TraceFile{}, fmt.Errorf("review trace event %d is invalid", i+1)
+		}
+	}
+	if trace.Events == nil {
+		trace.Events = []TraceEvent{}
+	}
+	return trace, nil
+}

+package review
+
+import (
+	"strings"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+func TestDecodeTraceFileIsPinnedAndBounded(t *testing.T) {
+	head := strings.Repeat("c", 40)
+	valid := `{"revision":"` + head + `","tier":"plus","spend":{"input_tokens":1,"output_tokens":1,"cost_microusd":1,"model_calls":1,"tool_calls":0},"events":[{"seq":1,"agent":"planner","kind":"model","name":"planner","elapsed_ms":3}]}`
+	if trace, err := DecodeTraceFile([]byte(valid), head); err != nil || len(trace.Events) != 1 {
+		t.Fatalf("trace=%#v err=%v", trace, err)
+	}
+	cases := map[string]string{
+		"stale":     strings.Replace(valid, head, strings.Repeat("d", 40), 1),
+		"base tier": strings.Replace(valid, `"plus"`, `"base"`, 1),
+		"bad kind":  strings.Replace(valid, `"kind":"model"`, `"kind":"shell"`, 1),
+		"bad seq":   strings.Replace(valid, `"seq":1`, `"seq":2`, 1),
+		"unknown":   strings.Replace(valid, `"elapsed_ms":3`, `"elapsed_ms":3,"raw_error":"x"`, 1),
+		"long":      strings.Replace(valid, `"name":"planner"`, `"name":"planner","detail":"`+strings.Repeat("x", MaxTraceDetailBytes+1)+`"`, 1),
+		"trailing":  valid + "{}",
+	}
+	for name, body := range cases {
+		if _, err := DecodeTraceFile([]byte(body), head); err == nil {
+			t.Fatalf("%s: accepted", name)
+		}
+	}
+}

explanations.title: Trace exports are revision-pinned
explanations.summary: The optional `--trace-file` is decoded against the report’s head revision before being attached. A stale or invalid trace therefore prevents export, while reports without the option remain unchanged.

explanations.title: Task outcomes join the trace
explanations.summary: When a runner has a trace configured, it adds each completed task’s outcome to the trace, including failed tasks, before delivering the partial result.

explanations.title: Trace records bounded review steps
explanations.summary: The recorder captures tool-call details and bounded result previews, but omits previews for issue lookups. It also records model-call usage and caps stored events, counting further events as dropped.

explanations.title: Imported traces are strictly validated
explanations.summary: Trace files are limited to supported tiers, event counts, and text sizes; event sequences must be ordered, and unknown fields or trailing data are rejected. This keeps imported trace data within the format the report can safely handle.

explanations.title: Reports display traces as inert text
explanations.summary: Reports show the trace section only when a trace is attached. It summarizes spend, exhausted budgets, dropped steps, and task outcomes, with the full event list expandable; trace strings are inserted as text rather than interpreted as markup.
